feedback.finish: The Maya priests were some of the most powerful and well-educated people in society. The Maya believed the priests could communicate directly with the gods.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

hint.label: Sacrifice
hint.text: A sacrifice is when an offering is made to a god.

atoms.text: Maya priests were responsible for leading ceremonies of worship and sacrifice. These ceremonies started with feasting and dancing, then offerings were made to the gods.

Food and incense were the most common offerings to the gods. More special offerings would have included animal sacrifice, bloodletting and even human sacrifice. Bloodletting involved priests and rulers cutting their ears or their tongues and offering up their blood as a ritual.
Human sacrifices were only carried out on special occasions because it was the highest form of praise possible to give the gods. The victims were usually enslaved people or prisoners of war.

feedback.finish: The Maya had several different methods of sacrificing people. Some were beheaded, others were shot with arrows and the most unlucky had their hearts cut out while they were still beating!

hint.label: Temple
hint.text: The temple is the small room on top of the pyramid.

feedback.finish: The temple was where religious ceremonies would take place. Only the priests, rulers and sacrificial victims were allowed to climb the pyramid steps up to the temple.
